title: Region and year resampling gave limits across zero for a ComCat late-share depth contrast in 2001-2024
abstract: We tested whether a reported earthquake timing contrast survives geographic resampling. We used a fixed USGS ComCat snapshot, 646 shallow and 99 deep M6.5 to below 8 centers in 2001-2024, and the earlier 200 km selection. The magnitude-adjusted deep-minus-shallow late-share contrast was 21.29 percentage points. Three-year block resampling gave 95% percentile limits of 11.18 to 36.12 points. Resampling occupied 20-degree cells and year blocks together gave limits of -15.51 to 51.50 points on the main grid. All three shifted grids also gave limits across zero. The main joint calculation had 273 undefined draws out of 9,999; limits use the remaining draws. Deep late pairs occurred in only five of 12 deep-center cells. This sensitivity test shows that year-only uncertainty does not describe geographic variation under these resampling models. It does not establish a null depth effect or calibrated population coverage. Sparse counts, grid choice, exchangeability assumptions, shared events, future-based selection and revised mixed-network magnitudes limit inference. Code, aggregate results, draws, provenance, a scalar count audit and a figure are included. External records stay outside the signed package.

display.caption: Magnitude-adjusted deep-minus-shallow late share. Bars are conditional 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of defined draws, not calibrated confidence intervals. Grid numbers give latitude and longitude offsets in degrees. Joint region/year limits cross zero on all four grids. The point estimate is unchanged.
